input: This is the third time I have asked about payment. The invoice is a month overdue and I need an answer today.
reply: Hi, I am following up for the third time on invoice #1048, which is now a month overdue. I understand things get busy, but I do need a clear answer today on when the payment will be sent, so I can plan my schedule. Thank you for understanding.
explanation: Firm but hedged: states the facts and a clear deadline, softened with understanding and thanks.

input: Long-term client asked for one small extra banner. I am happy to do it free this once but want to note it.
reply: Hi! Happy to add the extra banner for you this time — consider it on the house. Just flagging so we both keep track: anything beyond this one, I will pop into a quick estimate first. Sound good?
explanation: Positive politeness (generosity, shared understanding) lets a free favour set a boundary for next time.

input: Client praised my work and I want to thank them and ask for a testimonial.
reply: Hi, thank you so much — that genuinely made my day! I loved working on this project with you. If you have a moment, would you be happy to share a short testimonial I could use on my profile? No pressure at all, of course.
explanation: Reciprocates the warmth, then makes a low-pressure ask for a testimonial.

input: New client keeps sending small tweaks one by one instead of batching them. Need to ask for batched feedback.
reply: Hello, thanks for the notes. To keep the revisions efficient, could we batch the remaining tweaks into one list? That way I can apply them all in one round and we stay within the included revisions.
explanation: A process suggestion framed as a benefit to the client, hedged with a question.

input: Small delay of one day because I was ill, client is relaxed and flexible.
reply: Hi! Quick update — I was unwell yesterday, so the files will land tomorrow morning instead of tonight. Sorry for the tiny delay, and thanks as always for your flexibility. I will send them first thing.
explanation: Apology plus shared goodwill fits a close relationship and a one-day delay.

input: Client sent an angry message full of capital letters demanding the files immediately.
reply: Hello, I understand this is urgent and I appreciate you flagging it. The files will be ready by tomorrow morning — I am working on them now. If there is anything specific you need first, please let me know and I will prioritise it.
explanation: Acknowledges urgency, gives a concrete time, and offers a partial win — without matching the anger.

input: Client wants a refund for one milestone because they changed their mind about the feature, not because of quality.
reply: Hi, I understand plans change, and I appreciate you letting me know. Since that milestone was completed as agreed, I cannot refund it, but I am happy to put the same value toward the replacement feature instead. Would that work for you?
explanation: Validates the change of mind, refuses the refund, and redirects the value to the new work.

input: Client ghosted after I delivered the work and the final invoice is unpaid. Need a final follow-up before escalating.
reply: Hello, I am writing one last time about the final invoice, which is now 30 days overdue. I would really appreciate an update this week. If I do not hear back, I will need to consider next steps, which I would much rather avoid. Thank you for your attention.
explanation: Firm final notice: polite but explicit that escalation follows, with a face-saving preference to avoid it.

input: Client wants my personal phone number and WhatsApp for faster replies. I prefer to keep work on email.
reply: Hello, thanks for asking. I keep all project communication on email so nothing gets lost and we both have a record. I reply there within one working day — that is the fastest way to reach me.
explanation: Gives a practical reason (record-keeping) for the boundary instead of a personal refusal.

input: Regular client asks for a small discount on a big project as a loyal customer.
reply: Hi! Thanks for the loyalty — it genuinely means a lot. I can offer a 10% discount on this project as a thank-you. Shall I send the updated quote?
explanation: Warmth and gratitude make a small concession feel like a relationship gesture, not a negotiation loss.
